fields.h1: Build a Customer Information Form That Keeps One Record
fields.hero_description: Build a customer information form that matches returning customers and keeps each record current in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Customer Record Needs to Stay Useful
fields.features_subheading: A sheet filled in once is out of date by the next visit. Emergent builds the form and the record behind it, one entry per customer.
fields.feature_1:
Repeat visitors matched by phone number

The form asks for a phone number before anything else. When the number matches a customer already on file, the new answers update that record and the visit is added to its history.
fields.feature_2:
Billing and ship-to addresses kept apart

Customers who pay from one address and receive at another get a second address block. Leave the box checked and the form copies the billing address, so nobody types it twice.
fields.feature_3:
New accounts go to your accounting tool

The app connects to QuickBooks, Xero or any accounting tool with an API. Each new business customer is created there with its addresses and payables email, ready to invoice.
fields.feature_4:
A yearly link to confirm what is on file

Once a year, each customer gets an email with a link to their own record. They confirm it as it stands or fix what changed, and every edit lands on a list for the office to check.
fields.feature_5:
Contact preferences stored with the record

Each customer picks email or phone and the best time to call. The choice sits on the record beside the address, where whoever makes the next call can read it before dialing.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to your own servers

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when customer records need to sit next to your other systems. Host it where you like and keep changing it from there.

fields.tab_content_1:
On a Saturday with 18 check-ins, 11 were returning customers

Pellstone Auto Repair checks in walk-ins on a tablet that asks for the phone number first. A number already on file updates that customer's record instead of starting a second one. Last Saturday, 11 of 18 check-ins matched a record and 7 were new. Service writer Nikolai Brisbin sees each tagged Returning or New.
fields.tab_content_2:
Cobblecrest Cafe goes into QuickBooks with two addresses

Dunmere Coffee Roasters sells beans to cafes. Cobblecrest Cafe pays from Ternhill Street but takes deliveries on Marlowe Yard, between 7 and 10 a.m. The app creates the customer in QuickBooks with both addresses. Account manager Kalani Vukovic gets an email that a new account is in.
fields.tab_content_3:
In January, 31 of 340 plan customers sent a change

Each January, Gorsefield Heating emails its 340 maintenance plan customers a link to their record. So far, 212 confirmed it as it stands and 31 sent a change, such as a new phone or furnace. Those 31 wait on office manager Mariela Petrosyan's review list. The 97 with no answer get a reminder email after 14 days.
fields.tab_content_4:
With 4 sites under one account, each keeps its gate code

Hatchgate Properties pays Thistlebrook Pest Control on one invoice for 4 apartment buildings. The form takes billing contact Wendeline Asaro once, then each site with its gate code and parking note. Technician Ezekiel Tamm opens the Osier Court record on his route and has the gate code without calling the office.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Customer Information Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a customer information form that finds repeat customers by phone and asks each one to confirm their details yearly.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what you will do with each answer
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the phone number first
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick who hears about new customers
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what each answer is for before you add a field: the phone number to find returning customers, the address to bill or ship, the email for receipts. A field nobody uses makes the form longer and the record harder to keep current.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the phone number at the top so the form can check it against the records on file. A match updates the existing customer instead of creating a second entry, which keeps past visits and notes on one record.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Add a ship-to block for customers who receive orders somewhere other than where they pay. Default it to the billing address with a checkbox. A homeowner then fills in one address, and a cafe with a back-door delivery fills in two.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the person who acts on each new record and how they find out. A wholesale account might email the account manager, while a walk-in only needs a tag on the check-in list. Keep each alert to a short note and a link.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the record in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the fields, the phone number match, the addresses, and who gets notified, in plain English. It builds the form along with the customer database behind it. Change either one later with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test it as a returning customer
fields.howto_step_6_des: Submit the form twice with the same phone number and a new address the second time. You should see one record holding the new address, not two records. Then submit a number that is not on file and confirm a new record starts.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Set a yearly check on the records
fields.howto_step_7_des: Pick a month to email every customer a link to the record on file. Customers confirm it or correct it. Every change goes to one person to review before it replaces the old details, which keeps stale addresses from piling up.

faq_plan.q: What is a customer information form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a customer information form?

prov.original: What is a customer information form?

faq_plan.a: A customer information form is the form a business uses to record who a customer is and how to reach them. It asks for name, phone, email, and billing address, plus what the business needs to serve them, such as a vehicle or a delivery window. Each completed form becomes that customer's record.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a customer information form?
faq_plan.a: Decide which details you will act on, then describe the form in a prompt to Emergent's AI form builder: the fields, a phone number match for returning customers, and who hears about new ones. Emergent then builds it with a database behind it. Open the link on a counter tablet or send it to customers.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a customer information form include?
faq_plan.a: Start with name, phone, email, and a billing address, then add only what your business acts on. An auto shop adds the vehicle, a wholesaler adds a ship-to address and a payables contact, and a heating company adds the equipment on site. Make the phone number required if it is how you find returning customers.

faq_plan.q: Should staff or customers fill in the customer information form?
faq_plan.a: Either works with the same form. Customers typing on a tablet or a link spell their own names and emails, which cuts typos. When staff take the details over the phone, have them read each answer back. After training new hires on the form, a short check built from learning and development survey questions shows who needs another pass.

faq_plan.q: What if a customer fills out the customer information form twice?
faq_plan.a: Match on one field the customer always knows, such as the phone number, before the rest of the answers save. A match updates the record on file, and no match starts a new one. Add email as a second check for households that share a phone. With Emergent, those records live in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How often should customers update the details on their customer information form?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a full check once a year, and update single fields whenever a customer mentions a change at the counter or on a call. Send the yearly request in a quiet month, with a link customers can open and correct. Emergent puts no cap on responses, and the request can go to every customer on the list.

faq_plan.q: Should a customer information form ask how the customer found the business?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you will act on the answer. One dropdown with your real channels, such as a referral, a search, or the sign out front, shows where new customers come from without slowing the form. Keep deeper questions about who your customers are for a separate survey built from audience survey questions.

faq_plan.q: How should a customer information form handle a business with several locations?
faq_plan.a: Take the billing contact once, then let the customer add a block for each location with its address and access details. Give each location its own record under the one account. Name each location the way the customer names it on their invoices. Your crew and their office then mean the same building.

faq_plan.q: Can a customer information form add new customers to accounting software?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the form is connected to your accounting tool. Apps built with Emergent connect to any tool with an API. A submitted form can then create the customer there with billing details filled in. Map each form field to its matching field in the accounting tool and test one entry before going live.

faq_plan.q: Can a customer information form collect birthdays for a rewards program?
faq_plan.a: It can, once you add the question. Ask for the month and day only, mark the question optional, and say what customers get for answering. Store the date on the record so each month's birthday offers can go out from one list. Keep playful extras, such as game survey questions for a customer event, on a separate form.

plan.angle: The top results for customer information form are blank templates and printable sheets that collect a name, phone and address once and stop there. Nothing shows what happens to the record afterward: the same customer filled in twice, a wholesale account typed into the accounting system by hand, an address that went stale two years ago, a property manager with four sites crammed into one address line. This page is for the small business that keeps one record per customer: a form that matches returning customers by phone number, sends new wholesale accounts to the accounting system, asks plan customers to confirm their details once a year, and holds several service sites under one account. Intake questionnaires, credit applications and contact forms stay on their own pages.
